rationale: This is a single-denominator swap (lag dp → lag at) on the archive's best performer, Physical-Capital Payoff Balance Value, and the resulting Δoibdp/lag(at) leg is little more than the well-known profitability-change signal, so it is a cosmetic robustness variant rather than a new mechanism.

The expression simply grafts the valuation leg of the archived Cash-Backed/Physical-Capital family (che/mktcap) onto the quality leg of the archived SG&A-Payoff Cash Value, a pure recombination of two already-evaluated signals whose incremental information over che/mktcap × ROA is likely minimal.

It takes the valuation leg of the archived R&D-Budgeted Liquidity Franchise and the MIN(level, DELTA) intangible-ROA quality leg of the archived Liquidity-Backed Intangible Productivity, producing a highly parameterized hybrid of two already-tested signals with no genuinely new economic channel.

The internal-consistency fix (differencing post-depreciation rather than pre-depreciation profit) is a real accounting alignment improvement, and pairing it with the enterprise-level cash yield rather than balance-sheet cash tests whether the payoff mechanism survives a genuinely different valuation channel, though it remains a close relative of the archived winner.

This differs from the archived Cash-Burn-Protected Balance Value only by rescaling the cash-flow leg from at to dp, a mechanical denominator change that also reintroduces the low-depreciation distortion the proposal's own reasoning claims to guard against.

The conversion ratio pi/(|pi|+|oibdp|) is internally inconsistent with the stated hypothesis — it rewards pretax income being large relative to operating earnings, which flags non-operating gains and low depreciation/interest intensity as "efficient conversion" — and the ABS construction makes the measure non-monotone for loss firms while being largely collinear with the pi/at level leg.
